stimulus.text: The Capitol in 1800. The drawing, titled “THE CAPITOL IN 1800,” shows the north wing of the Capitol in Washington, with tall classical columns, arched windows, and a flat roofline, standing nearly alone on open ground, with a few low unfinished buildings in the distance. The federal government moved to the new capital at Washington in 1800.
stimulus.source_note: The Capitol in 1800, from Glenn Brown, History of the United States Capitol, plate 38, Library of Congress. Public domain.

stem: The drawing shows the Capitol in 1800 as...

options.text: a large classical building standing mostly alone on open ground.
a small wooden house hidden among trees.
options.misconception: The building is large and made of stone, standing in the open.

options.text: a crowded city block full of shops and houses.
options.misconception: Only a few low buildings appear in the distance; the ground around the Capitol is open.

options.text: a domed building finished in every detail.
options.misconception: The drawing shows a flat roofline and unfinished buildings nearby, with no dome.

rationales.A: The drawing shows the large north wing with columns, standing nearly alone on open ground.
rationales.B: The building is large and stone, not a small wooden house.
rationales.C: The ground around it is open, with only a few low buildings far off.
rationales.D: The roofline is flat, with no dome, and buildings nearby are unfinished.
rationales.general:
1. The drawing is titled “THE CAPITOL IN 1800.”
2. It shows a large building with tall columns and arched windows.
3. The ground around it is open, with only a few low buildings in the distance.
4. So the Capitol appears as a large classical building standing mostly alone.
Remember: describe the building and its setting as the drawing shows them.
